title: Certificates of Deposit: The Sum Accepted When the Owner Asks to Add as Much as Possible
content:
When a certificate holder asks to place, into a PCB certificate from the Certificates of Deposit line, as much as the certificate will take as an in-term add-on, several limits each leave some room. This page states how those rooms combine into the one sum accepted, and when nothing is accepted.

## How the rooms combine

The sum accepted is the smallest of three rooms, each taken at the moment of the deposit: the room under the term total, the room under the tier's largest principal, and the room in the savings or money market account the money comes from. That smallest room is rounded half-up to 2 decimal places, and the rounded figure is the sum accepted.

## When nothing is accepted

No add-on is accepted, and nothing is written, if any of the following is true:

- the certificate lacks the standing an in-term add-on needs;
- the term's in-term add-on count is already exhausted;
- the smallest room, once rounded, is below the tier's smallest in-term add-on.

The customer-wide principal concentration ceiling applies to the add-on as well, and it works by refusal: an add-on that would break that ceiling is declined, not cut down to fit.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures; the tier's smallest in-term add-on is assumed to be USD 250.00 for illustration)

| Room under the term total | Room under the largest principal | Room in the source account | Sum accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD 20000.00 | USD 505000.00 | USD 18250.40 | USD 18250.40, the smallest room |
| USD 12500.00 | USD 505000.00 | USD 40000.00 | USD 12500.00 |
| USD 20000.00 | USD 10000.00 | USD 40000.00 | USD 10000.00 |
| USD 20000.00 | USD 505000.00 | USD 180.00 | nothing; USD 180.00 is below the smallest add-on |
| count exhausted | any | any | nothing |
